model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the "effect" values across different language families for five model variants. The horizontal axis represents language family categories, labeled from left to right as IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis represents "effect" on a linear scale ranging from approximately −5 to 30, with major tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, five grouped bars are displayed side by side, corresponding to the models XLM-L₂ (blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red/pink), and XLM-B₂ (red), as indicated in the legend. Each bar includes error bars representing variability. For IE-Baltic, all five bars are relatively small, ranging from approximately 1 to 5. For IE-Germanic, XLM-L₂ reaches roughly 10, mBERT-R₂ is near 0, XLM-R₂ is slightly negative, and mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ are approximately 8 and 15, respectively. IE-Indic shows the tallest bars overall, with mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ reaching approximately 18–21, and mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ at roughly 24 and 21. IE-Romance bars range from about 1 to 13, with mBERT-B₂ being the tallest in that group. IE-Slavic shows values from roughly 3 to 18, with mBERT-B₂ reaching the highest. IE-other has bars ranging from about 1 to 8. Isolate shows very small bars, all near zero or slightly negative. Semitic displays notable variation, with XLM-L₂ at approximately 11, mBERT-R₂ near −1, XLM-R₂ near −2, and mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ at roughly 5 and 12. Uralic bars are all near zero or slightly negative, with large error bars. The bars are not sorted by value but are arranged by language family grouping, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized beyond the color coding.
